thesis: Use linked operating metrics to manage business value, retention and cash survival.
summary: Seven principles cover saleable value, gross margin, retention, customer value, acquisition cost, funnel conversion and runway. Martell illustrates revenue-minus-delivery-cost gross profit, churn and revenue-based LTV, CAC by paying customers, cash payback and stage-level conversion. Daily cash reporting is intended to expose problems before a retrospective P&L.

insights.title: Separate delivery economics from total profit
insights.explanation: He explicitly distinguishes gross profit from revenue less all expenses; interpreting it still requires consistent cost definitions.

insights.explanation: A large lifetime value does not remove a near-term cash deficit when acquisition costs are recovered slowly.

review_status: Codex editorial draft; complete local transcript read; claims not independently verified
synthesis_method: Direct Codex extraction from complete local transcript; exact quotations verified locally
context_and_limits: Educational approximations contain errors. $1.5m revenue at 30% is $450k, not $500k. He verbally says cash minus burn for runway, while his worked $100k/$20k example correctly divides to get five months. Revenue/churn LTV omits margin, discounting and varying retention; gross margin differs from net cash. A 70% margin or 3% monthly churn is not a universal target. Simplified profit multiples do not determine actual enterprise/equity value, debt or transaction proceeds.
review_changes: Adds formula and arithmetic qualifications, distinguishes gross profit from cash and treats industry-wide benchmarks as personal heuristics rather than rules.
